sources.title: The Starry Night Accurately Depicts a Scientific Theory That Wasn't Described Until Years After van Gogh's Death
Turbulent skies of Vincent Van Gogh's The Starry Night may align with a scientific theory

facts.text: Van Gogh completed The Starry Night in June 1889, during his year-long stay at the asylum in Saint-Rémy in southern France.
The painting reflects the countryside he saw from his window, by day and at night, combined with his own vision.
The Starry Night is held by the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
In the 1940s, Andrei Kolmogorov laid a foundation of modern turbulence theory, describing how large eddies break into smaller ones in a predictable way.
In 2006, physicists in Mexico found that the patterns of brightness in The Starry Night match Kolmogorov's description of turbulence.
A 2024 study led by Yongxiang Huang found that 14 swirls in the painting fit Kolmogorov's theory and that small brushstrokes match Batchelor scaling.
Van Gogh died 13 years before Kolmogorov was born, so he could not have known the theory.
Scientists caution that a still painting is not a moving fluid and that it is unclear whether the match is a coincidence; some suggest van Gogh closely observed clouds and the sky.
